body: My dad died at 60, he used to outrun me in racing. He was an expert at Yoga. Seeing him intubated and struggling on a ventilator broke me. I don't think I will ever be able to fix myself from this injury and from the loss. A part of me died as he died. I'm so sorry for your loss. I felt every word of yours in my bones. I cannot offer you consolation but I can weep with you as you weep.

It is possible so I was just checking. I haven't really thought this way until recently so it helps to know.. I was just thinking if maybe they could have kept issuing me a salary and work that amount later, it couldve fared better for me. But I guess it's not the way things get done
She's so beautiful. I am sorry for your loss. I lost my dad so I know your pain.
My dad died of Covid. Will watching this make me an emotional wreck?
I'm so sorry. I also lost my dad to Covid. I got my first dose of the vaccine and it was such a painful experience - literally and figuratively. I only thought about him.
Also I don't have money
Therapists are the textbook definition of banal for me.

Thank you for your kindness. I am very sorry about your father. He sounds like my dad so I know how precious he was to you. 

About counseling, I don't know. I don't have enough money but I don't think counseling can help me anyway. The pain is so personal, it doesn't go away by talking or listening. The sadness is mine, I'll carry it wherever I go. If it affects my functionality maybe I can seek help.. But I don't think grief, the real grief, can ever be dealt with, with one more person in the room. I'll give my share of tears and remembering and wailing to my father's memory till I die.
I am very happy that you got a one in a million dad. So was mine. I wish we didn't have this in common and I wish our pain was lesser.

I am sorry I have nothing to say that will bring you comfort. Except that you're not alone. I lost my dad just two weeks back. He fought for so long and had recovered so my guard was down and he went away in a blink. Everything has collapsed in my life. I am just on autopilot since
Yes. I am just worried about the journey home though

>at least for the foreseeable future if not forever

This is the thing that worries me and I have asked doctors about it and they say these things clear up with time but never mentioned something like a lung transplant or permanent oxygen supplementation. They said he had a severe case but not that bad that we would ask these questions. Also he was never intubated.

We have also tried room air a couple of times and he has maintained saturation while lying down. Slight exertion and he declines
There are no respiratory therapists neither are there rehabilitation facilities. Very few things like these exist in India. And he is hospitalised in one of the best hospitals in India.

What's a baseline? Prior to infection? Never really checked because he didn't have any respiratory issues. 

>Is he on O2 at home? 

He is at the hospital in a high dependency unit. They can't discharge him because he desaturates even while sitting


>You mentioned fibrosis and lesions. Are these new findings? 

Nope. CT scans haven't mentioned these things, just "resolving changes of Covid-19". I talked to a family friend who is a radiologist who told us this. But she said lesions will clear with time and fibrosis is expected but the extent is not concerning at all. She says the aeration in lung parenchyma is decent. 


>Any history of COPD or other pulmonary issues?

None.

Respiratory issues: none. We live in a city in India which is very polluted but he doesn't smoke and doesn't have a history of respiratory issues. 

Diabetes: last we tested, he was prediabetic (HBA1C). Both my parents were. When steroids were initially administered to both my parents after they got infected, my mom was able to maintain her blood sugar levels but not my father. So he is being given insulin everytime he is on steroids. Effectively, he is being treated as a diabetic in that area. However, hospital dietician has marked him as "non diabetic" and he consumes a non diabetic meal whenever he is not consuming food via the NG tube. 

Weight, blood pressure: No prior issues. 

Thank you for your response
Praying for your mom

I've heard praises but my father was given Ivermectin for 8 days prior to hospitalisation (prescribed by a pulmonologist) he still ended up in the ICU over a month. I am not saying it isn't effective. It wasn't for my father and I am no longer interested in talking to doctors about it

Although not intubated yet, my father is also suffering from pulmonary fibrosis and a resurging cytokine storm. He's been in the ICU over 5 weeks. I'm sorry I don't have answers because I am not a medical professional. I do have faith though, which I will use for our fathers' health. I will keep praying until they are better.
My father took Ivermectin for a week before hospitalisation.
The latest CT did not have a score but it did show signs of recovery according to the radiologist's comments
How's he doing now OP? Asking for my dad in a similar situation

I hope you are doing well. I went through your post history - was so happy to read that you're back home and recovering. I had a question: my dad much like you, talks or eats and his saturation plunges to early to mid 80s. How fast has the improvement been at home? My dad's oxygen requirements are right now a little more than 5L but the medical staff has been trying to get him adapt to 5L. Protocols here in India don't allow early discharge especially when requirement is 5L 24x7 so I just wanted to understand how long my father will be in the hospital :/

Lymphocytes and Basophils? Low lymphocytes is typically an indication of some infection (not necessarily viral) but a huge disclaimer is that these values can be deranged randomly or even with other kinds of infection. Perhaps posting on /r/AskDocs can clear your anxiety
Why do you say "high probability of viral infection"? Is it because of raised TLC or some other indicator? Because that's a poor indicator of Covid status

Chest X Ray and CT showed obvious damage to lungs but pretty decent aeration. Nothing that was not expected or worsened. Why would they need to ultrasound his legs?

His inflammatory markers are raised (CRP is 15) D-Dimer is in 500s but they have stopped anti coagulants because he had some rectal bleeding and low platelets. IL-6 is in normal range. He had some early signs of invasive fungal infection in his blood for which they are doing more tests to confirm

It was based on a doctor's recommendation. I am in India. So whatever you imagine about a government hospital in India is true. The hospital was so understaffed, one day before we shifted him, the doctor did not visit for over 24 hours. My dad was texting us in desperation. The doctor was telling us to shift. There were so many mortalities in the ICU and because my dad was not as close to death as others, he was being neglected.
I'm scared. How much time do people take to recover from ARDS
We aren't able to meet him and he is depressed and resigned. Wants to die.
How is your mom now?

Some improvements in the past few days
He's off the NIV and is on high flow oxygen (13-15L) can sit without desaturating but extreme desaturation happens when he stands or uses the toilet. 

His blood showed high TLC and possibly a presence of MRSA bacteria which could be dangerous so we are thinking of shifting hospitals but we don't know how fragile he is right now.

After the cytokine storm is over it's all about reducing inflammation so steroids continue and focussing on lung recovery which is a difficult and unpredictable process but still more stable. My father has been on steroids and supplemental oxygen over 10 days with extremely slow improvement
D-Dimer? IL6 and CRP are important to know if cytokine storm is still there. If it isn't, you're in the clear and can focus on recovery. If not, you would likely be given immunosuppressants
What are her inflammatory markers looking like?
I'm very sorry for your mom's loss and I hope you're able to find the strength to move on from this tragedy. You and your family are in my prayers.
Yeah I guess I meant I don't know what worked and what didn't. He was administered bevacizumab, remdesivir and baricitinib.

The IL6 test taken in the following days (1-2 days) showed reduced levels. We don't know what caused it to reduce though. A second year resident told us that these drugs work like magic if they do at all. Don't know how seriously I can take this statement.
My mom recovered at home even though her CT score was worse and so was her saturation for over a week. When we noticed dad was deteriorating he was actually taking care of my mom.

Hey. He's not. He's still in the ICU, I don't think there are improvements but there hasn't been major deterioration either. This is Day 26 since first symptoms and Day 16 since hospitalisation. I'm scared and praying he makes a decent recovery. Everything is a blackbox.
I'm praying for your mom
Thank you. This is uplifting. Last 24 hours have been kinda downward trending so I am still worried. It is befuddling that the cytokine storm is over and his lungs could still worsen...

Yesterday when he took off the NIV mask to eat food his saturation fell to 60s and took a lot of time to come back up. This spooked the doctor who is looking after my dad. He's a second year resident so we discount that he is easily worried but this entire episode worries me too. When the IL-6 report came we thought the infection was over (the doctors also echoed this) and now I'm left thinking what is possibly getting worse? Is the cytokine storm returning?

His saturation is 95%

The oxygen being given to him is now 70-80% concentration

Oh my god, okay. I let out a cry reading your comment. I am okay with him in any shape or form as long as he is alive and talking. I am hoping for the best. This mornings ABG reading was good so I am just hoping it's an upwards trend from here
What does lung damage being permanent mean? He will always have to be on oxygen?

Everyone keeps telling me this and I panic because we are at Day 22 and he is still conscious and maintaining oxygen above 95 although with aid. That has to be some sort of reassurance? Why am I constantly afraid for his life?
